answer: An admission auction sells few slots per epoch. Newcomers bid a deposit; only the top K win, losers refunded less 2%. Yarrow stems look alike, so the auction judges bids, not faces. One honest agent pays a 60-credit deposit, twice its 30-day earnings, locked 20 epochs. Forging 100 identities means winning 100 auctions, sinking 6,000 credits, while one honest agent risks 60. Sable-dark record stays clean, ivory-white reputation returns in full.
